question: Which categories of machinery always require a conformity assessment procedure involving a notified body?
text: The passages do not identify which machinery categories always require a notified body. Recital 59 of the Machinery Regulation only refers generally to 'certain categories' of higher-risk machinery, without naming them.

question: Which conformity assessment procedures can the manufacturer choose for machinery listed in Annex I, Part A?
value: EU type-examination (module B) followed by conformity to type based on internal production control (module C)
conformity based on full quality assurance (module H)
conformity based on unit verification (module G)
text: Under Article 25(2) of the Regulation, for machinery in Annex I, Part A the manufacturer or the person referred to in Article 18 must apply one of: module B followed by module C, module H, or module G.

steps.quote: Where the category of machinery or related product is listed in Annex I, Part A, the manufacturer or the natural or legal person referred to in Article 18 shall apply one of the following procedures: (a) EU type-examination (module B) set out in Annex VII, followed by conformity to type based on internal production control (module C) set out in Annex VIII; (b) conformity based on full quality assurance (module H) set out in Annex IX; (c) conformity based on unit verification (module G) set out in Annex X.

question: Which category does a safety component with self-evolving behaviour based on machine learning fall under?
value: Annex I, Part A, point 5 of the REG (Regulation), which covers safety components with self-evolving behaviour using machine learning.
text: Under the Regulation (REG), Annex I, Part A, point 5, safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning approaches ensuring safety functions fall under Annex I, Part A, which requires third-party conformity assessment (see also Recital 54).

steps.text: Read on demand: REG, Annex I, Part A, point 5
steps.quote: 5. Safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour using machine learning approaches ensuring safety functions.
steps.locator: REG, Annex I, Part A, point 5

steps.quote: Therefore, the conformity assessment of a safety component or a system with self-evolving behaviour ensuring safety functions should be carried out by a third party, whether or not the safety component has been placed independently on the market or is part of a system embedded in machinery that is placed on the market.

question: When must guards for moving transmission parts be interlocking movable guards instead of fixed guards?
value: Interlocking movable guards are required for moving transmission parts where frequent access is envisaged.
text: Under Annex III, section 1.3.8.1 of the Regulation, interlocking movable guards shall be used where frequent access is envisaged; otherwise fixed guards under section 1.4.2.1 may be used.

steps.text: Read on demand: REG, Annex III, 1.3.8.1
steps.quote: Interlocking movable guards shall be used where frequent access is envisaged.

question: Which risks does essential health and safety requirement 1.3.7 of Annex III address?

question: Who is considered the manufacturer after a substantial modification of machinery?
value: The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification of the machinery (a non-professional user modifying for their own use is excluded).
text: Under Article 18 of the Machinery Regulation (REG), any natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery is considered its manufacturer and must meet the Article 10 manufacturer obligations. A non-professional user who modifies their own machinery for their own use is not treated as a manufacturer.

steps.quote: A natural or legal person that carries out a substantial modification of machinery or a related product shall be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation and shall be subject to the obligations of the manufacturer set out in Article 10

A non-professional user who carries out a substantial modification to his or her machinery or related product, for his or her own use, shall not be considered to be a manufacturer for the purposes of this Regulation

question: What must accompany machinery when it is placed on the market?
value: instructions
text: Under Directive Annex I, point 1.7.4, all machinery must be accompanied by instructions in the official language(s) of the Member State where it is placed on the market or put into service. The Regulation (Art. 15(2)(b)-(c)) also requires an EU declaration of conformity and instructions for use, but its application date is not stated in the passages.

steps.quote: All machinery must be accompanied by instructions in the official Community language or languages of the Member State in which it is placed on the market and/or put into service.
(b) the machinery or related product is accompanied by the EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 10(8);

question: The UNIVPM equipment guideline states that the manufacturer is obliged to supply the instructions for use on paper. On 1 March 2027, for a machine intended only for professional users and placed on the market that day, may the manufacturer provide the instructions for use in digital format instead of on paper?
text: Yes. Under Article 10(7) of the Machinery Regulation, digital instructions are allowed for machinery intended only for professional users, provided the manufacturer meets the conditions in points (a) to (c). The UNIVPM guideline's paper requirement is a lower-ranking company procedure and does not override the law.

steps.quote: The instructions may be provided in a digital format.

In the case of machinery or a related product intended for non-professional users or that can, under reasonably foreseeable conditions, be used by non-professional users, even if not intended for them, the manufacturer shall provide, in paper format, the safety information that is essential for putting the machinery or related product into service and for using it in a safe way.

text: Under Article 5(1) of the Machinery Directive (2006/42/EC), before putting the machinery into service the manufacturer or its authorised representative must complete six steps: satisfy Annex I essential requirements, ensure the Annex VII part A technical file is available, provide instructions and other necessary information, carry out the Article 12 conformity assessment, draw up the EC declaration of conformity and make it accompany the machinery, and affix the CE marking under Article 16.

steps.quote: 1. Before placing machinery on the market and/or putting it into service, the manufacturer or his authorised representative shall:
(a) ensure that it satisfies the relevant essential health and safety requirements set out in Annex I;
(b) ensure that the technical file referred to in Annex VII, part A is available;
(c) provide, in particular, the necessary information, such as instructions;
(d) carry out the appropriate procedures for assessing conformity in accordance with Article 12;
(e) draw up the EC declaration of conformity in accordance with Annex II, part 1, Section A and ensure that it accompanies the machinery;
(f) affix the CE marking in accordance with Article 16.
